      <title>Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story</link>
      <description><p>After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’</p><p>The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.</p><p>Kundizeza’s story <a href="https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a4f3fb6a6178e0225b39a4c/t/6a95fffc36f1fc568e02f7fe/1788215293124/3.The+Blue+Fighter.pdf">The Blue Fighter</a>, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families</p><p>The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.</p><p>The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">found the cult leader guilty</a> of the crimes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/storm-charles-floods-flight-cancellations-southern-europe-weather</link>
      <description><p>Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week </p><p>Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.</p><p>After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/storm-charles-floods-flight-cancellations-southern-europe-weather">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Remains believed to have belonged to Africans or Afro-Brazilians repatriated after being flown back by diplomats </p><p>Two skulls, including that of a man believed to have taken part in Brazil’s greatest slave revolt but whose remains were taken to the United States and used in racist eugenics studies at Harvard University, were repatriated on Wednesday.</p><p>The remains had been outside Brazil since the 19th century.       <title>Thursday briefing: What we do (and don’t) know about Alice Huang and the Nvidia affair</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/12/thursday-briefing-what-we-do-and-dont-know-about-alice-huang-and-the-nvidia-affair</link>
      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: US intelligence reportedly believes the former tech executive was recruited by Beijing, raising questions about the security of the AI industry and Trump’s close ties to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang</p><p></p><p>Good morning. Espionage is supposed to be a secretive business, and spies are supposed to be virtually invisible. That hasn’t been the case for Alice Huang, the mysterious Shanghai executive who formed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia, one of America’s most powerful tech companies.</p><p>Many questions have arisen since it emerged that US intelligence believes that Huang (no relation of Jensen’s) is an asset recruited by the Chinese intelligence services to spy on behalf of Beijing. This morning’s newsletter explains what we know about the story, and what it tells us about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage. That’s after the headlines.</p><p><em><strong>UK </strong></em>| Ministers are considering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/11/tv-entertainment-industry-protect-women-david-walliams-allegations-nandy">changing the law</a> to force the entertainment industry to better protect women and children in the wake of the revelations over David Walliams and the conviction of Russell Brand.</p><p><em><strong>Climate </strong></em>| The UK government has <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/11/uk-appoints-worlds-first-special-representative-for-climate-security">appointed the world’s first </a>special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country.</p><p><em><strong>US midterms </strong></em>| Democrat Scott Colom has become the first Black senator in Mississippi to be elected since Reconstruction,<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/11/scott-colom-mississippi-senate-race"> in a stunning upset </a>after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states.</p><p><em><strong>Europe </strong></em>| Millions of people across Spain have joined the country’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/11/spain-general-strike-housing-costs">first general strike in 14 years</a>, setting up picket lines to protest against soaring housing prices before an election in which the far right could be catapulted into power.</p><p><em><strong>Technology </strong></em>| Police officers <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/facial-recognition-errors-put-ethnic-minorities-at-risk-of-wrongful-arrest-police-watchdog-warns">risk arresting innocent people</a>, especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, an official report has found.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/12/thursday-briefing-what-we-do-and-dont-know-about-alice-huang-and-the-nvidia-affair">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b76023068afd6989a4d83782e8ad21ac88094570/335_0_3331_2666/master/3331.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=ae6e7cc781873a609353d81df20f9e53">

      <title>Children’s exposure to home wood-burning could be as significant as traffic exhaust, study suggests</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/wood-burning-stoves-pollution-traffic-exhaust-children</link>
      <description><p>Research finds highest levels of cancer-related PAH pollutants in cities that have widespread wood heating</p><p>Children’s exposure to home wood-burning could be as significant as exposure to traffic exhaust, suggests <a href="https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0013935126019742?via%3Dihub">new research</a> across six European towns and cities.</p><p>Scientists measured the air in buildings where children spend much of their time; in schools, sports centres and homes. Specifically, they looked at polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons <a href="https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2020.562813/full">(PAH)</a>, <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/benzoapyrene-properties-incident-management-and-toxicology/benzoapyrene-or-pahs-toxicological-overview">a family of pollutants</a> that are given off when fuels are burned.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/wood-burning-stoves-pollution-traffic-exhaust-children">Continue reading...</a></description>

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>

French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99b61d02-c596-11f1-9bf5-777190d2ada5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:50:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered food market</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-fire-burns-down-paris-s-oldest-covered-food-market</link><description>
A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5504c60-c610-11f1-b48e-936bba59cf88</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:02:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg">© Creative Commons</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French police clash with teens blockading schools as unions stage day of protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-french-police-clash-with-teens-blockading-schools-as-union-stage-day-of-protests</link><description>
French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/13/global-microsoft-outage-what-happened-and-why</link>
      <description><p>Problem affects businesses, government agencies and even tech firm’s own employees</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/13/microsoft-outage-outlook-teams-word-excel-reports">Microsoft scrambles to fix global outage affecting Teams and Outlook</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/live/2026/nov/13/microsoft-outage-down-today-live-update-outlook-teams-365-when-fixed-latest-status-cause-news">Microsoft outage – live updates</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/13/tell-us-have-you-been-affected-by-the-microsoft-outage">Tell us: have you been affected by the Microsoft outage?</a></p></li></ul><p>Millions of people were unable to access their emails, Teams chats or meetings on Thursday night and Friday morning after a Microsoft 365 outage brought down services across the globe.</p><p>The incident affected businesses, government agencies and even Microsoft employees. Businesses, government agencies and vital services around the world have all reported issues, from the US House of Representatives to an Australian spy agency and airlines in India. In the UK, police services, ambulances and hospitals reported issues with email services and online form submissions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/13/global-microsoft-outage-what-happened-and-why">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/jensen-huang-affair-timeline</link>
      <description><p>CEO behind the meteoric rise of Nvidia stepped down after it was revealed he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy </p><p>Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/nvidia">Nvidia</a>, the company at the center of the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/artificialintelligenceai">AI</a> boom, after leading it for more than 30 years.</p><p>Huang, an electrical engineer by education, stewarded the company from a $1bn firm when it went public in 1999 to a company valued at more than $4tn in 2026. But in a matter of days, after it was revealed he had an extramarital affair with a woman that US officials believe to be a Chinese spy, Huang managed to wipe more than $600bn from the company’s valuation.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/jensen-huang-affair-timeline">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/12/starbucks-workers-campus-rally-contract-talks</link>
      <description><p>Rallies will take place on more than US 40 campuses as workers seeking better pay and conditions decry stalled talks</p><p>Starbucks baristas, students, elected officials and allies are planning rallies at <a href="https://starbucksworkersunited.controlshift.app/events?link_id=2&amp;can_id=debd8d2ad19f005d15f9bbdff314d42a&amp;source=email-nov-12-day-of-action-for-starbucks-baristas&amp;email_referrer=email_3490793&amp;email_subject=nov-12-day-of-action-for-starbucks-baristas&amp;&amp;">over 40 college campuses</a> across the US on Thursday to support the Starbucks Workers United <a href="https://www.boycottstarbucks.net/">boycott campaign</a> as the union nears five years of deadlock with the company over contract negotiations.</p><p>Starbucks Workers United is <a href="https://sbworkersunited.org/what-were-fighting-for-updates-on-contract-bargaining/">seeking</a> better pay and stronger staffing levels, including a $17 an hour minimum wage for baristas and a minimum staffing of three workers per store. It has called on the public to <a href="https://www.boycottstarbucks.net/">boycott</a> Starbucks until its first contract is reached.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/12/starbucks-workers-campus-rally-contract-talks">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Sales of built units fell to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, with mortgage rates at nearly three-year high</p><p>US existing home sales hit a 16-year low in October as buyers were driven away by record-high <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/mortgage-rates">mortgage rates</a> and rising inflation, according to new data released on Wednesday.</p><p>Sales of already built units dropped to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) reported. The median existing-home sales price increased slightly to $416,700.       <description><p>Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit</p><p>Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case.       <description><p>Safety campaigners have condemned it and owners have complained about it. Goodbye to a steel monstrosity seemingly designed by a five-year-old</p><p>Elon Musk is having a rough go of it, isn’t he? The world’s richest man spent almost half a billion dollars on the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/04/elon-musk-midterm-spending-analysis">midterms</a> in a failed attempt to defend Republican control of government. Now the tech mogul, who moved from California to Texas to escape Democrats and regulations, finds himself in a newly blue state. He also finds himself the subject of an unflattering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/musk-review-epic-study-worlds-richest-most-banal-man-elon-film">documentary</a> and, if the Democrats follow through on threats to investigate him, could potentially be in a spot of legal bother.</p><p>And to top it all off? Musk’s beloved Cybertruck, the steel monstrosity that looks as if it were designed by a five-year-old, is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/06/tesla-to-wind-down-cybertruck-production-as-elon-musk-focuses-on-robotics-and-ai">winding down production</a>. According to Musk, this isn’t because it’s an abject failure, but because he is channelling his energy into other things. “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” Musk <a href="https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2119691615774146614?a=pN3ISFVZZ-aU4_-TlJw&amp;s=20">tweeted</a> on Monday. “But rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” (The Cybercab is a two-passenger robotaxi.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>A citizen referendum, only the second of its kind in Georgia history, seeks to block a zoning amendment</p><p>Ire Gene Grovner stood behind his house on a recent morning, between chicken pens on one side and rows of winter collard greens on the other, holding a knife and skinning a raccoon splayed across a wood post.</p><p>“The meat is good roasted,” Grovner said.       <title>It’s Happy Harry Kane day as England’s finest seizes his moment in style | Barney Ronay</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/happy-harry-kane-day-englands-finest-seizes-his-moment-croatia-nations-league</link>
      <description><p>The Ballon d’Or validated the forward’s career and he extended his incredible record for England with yet another goal on his 126th appearance</p><p>Happy Harry Kane day! And many happy Harry returns. There is a process in clinical psychology known as semantic satiation. Subjects are asked to repeat a word or phrase so many times that it loses any kind of meaning. Suddenly “daffodils” is just an absurd, empty set of sounds. So it was in the buildup to Harry Kane’s record-breaking 126th cap, at the end of Harry Kane Ballon d’Or fortnight, as Harry Kane’s England were led out by top scorer Harry Kane, climax to a week of Harry Kane tributes, Harry Kane montages, 26-page Harry Kane … wait. Where were we?</p><p>This was that kind of occasion from start to finish, a night where you expected to look up from your desk mid-match to see Kane’s head looming helpfully over your shoulder, to enter the Wembley toilets at half-time and find him silently offering you a breath mint and a scented tissue.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/happy-harry-kane-day-englands-finest-seizes-his-moment-croatia-nations-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Why Chelsea and Manchester City’s WSL clash is not as season-defining as you think</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/why-chelsea-and-manchester-citys-wsl-clash-is-not-as-season-defining-as-you-think</link>
      <description><p>Neither side have lost in the league yet but a more competitive division should take title race to the wire</p><p>There was a time when the games between the top three – traditionally Chelsea, Manchester City and Arsenal – were title-deciding games. Where every point taken off a title rival was key. Such was the gap in investment and quality between those teams and the rest of the Women’s Super League that it was extremely rare that points would be dropped to teams outside that elite clique.</p><p>As the WSL has grown in investment, profile and size, that narrative has started to shift a little. The investment gap is still large from the top to the bottom of the league, but increased investment among the “best of the rest” and even among those teams further down the table, as well as an increase in high-quality coaches with the tactical and technical vision to get more from players, is having an impact.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/why-chelsea-and-manchester-citys-wsl-clash-is-not-as-season-defining-as-you-think">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/football-association-art-prize</link>
      <description><p>Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival</p><p>It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player<em>.</em> You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England <em>– </em>at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball.</p><p>These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/football-association-art-prize">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Pierre Sage’s failure to fix defensive flaws leaves Crystal Palace seeking new solution</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/pierre-sage-sacked-manager-crystal-palace-steve-parish-premier-league</link>
      <description><p>A losing run, set-piece struggles and a call for help led Steve Parish to cut ties with the manager after five months</p><p>The moment that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/08/crystal-palace-liverpool-premier-league-match-report">summed up Crystal Palace’s season</a> under Pierre Sage came five minutes before half-time at Selhurst Park on Sunday. After Palace had gone close to taking the lead on numerous occasions against Liverpool, the Frenchman must have feared the worst when Alexis Mac Allister headed in from a soft free-kick conceded by Jefferson Lerma. The TV cameras immediately panned to Steve Parish in the stands. After the Palace chair removed his hands from in front of his eyes, his expression said everything you needed to know. The only surprise was that Sage had to wait until Thursday before his inevitable <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/pierre-sage-sacked-crystal-palace-manager-thomas-frank">fate was confirmed</a>.</p><p>Not since the start of the 2017-18 season, after Frank de Boer was appointed as Palace’s first permanent foreign manager and sacked after five matches, have the club found themselves bottom. In their record 14th consecutive season in the top flight, and with preliminary work having started on building a new £200m main stand despite major doubts over funding, Palace cannot afford to be relegated.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/pierre-sage-sacked-manager-crystal-palace-steve-parish-premier-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>Tottenham full-back to make 102nd appearance on Friday</p></li><li><p>‘It’s another reason to honour one of the greatest players’</p></li></ul><p>Andy Robertson insists his matching of Kenny Dalglish’s Scotland cap record by no means brings reputational parity.       <description><p>Argentinian oversaw high-scoring games in his one Chelsea season and Opta predicts his Manchester United side will move upfield quicker than that team</p><p>Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/aug/02/premier-league-managers-arteta-alonso-de-zerbi-carrick-klopp-guardiola">big beasts</a>” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager.</p><p>Pochettino took over Southampton midway through their first season back in the top flight (2012-13) after the club spent seven years in the lower leagues. In his only full campaign, they finished eighth.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/fifa-kozo-tashima-seeks-change-of-tone</link>
      <description><p>Japan FA honorary president is hoping a calmer approach that makes fewer unwelcome headlines for Fifa will be welcomed by football</p><p>Not many remember Japan’s bid for the 2022 World Cup, when the country finished the race with only two of the final 22 votes. Kozo Tashima was involved then, and now the honorary president of the Japan Football Association is going it alone in the hope of ousting Gianni Infantino.</p><p>The 68-year-old Tashima is an unlikely insurgent and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/05/japan-fa-head-kozo-tashima-stand-against-gianni-infantino-for-fifa-president">an unlikely challenger</a> to Infantino. He is, however, a familiar and respected figure in Asian and global football politics, and ready to take the Fifa presidency out of the headlines into a quieter era.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/fifa-kozo-tashima-seeks-change-of-tone">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>USSF cites state department advisory about Qatar</p></li><li><p>Competition set to kick off in eight days</p></li></ul><p>The US men’s national team have pulled out of the Fifa U-17 World Cup, which is due to kick off in Qatar in just over a week.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/michael-carrick-manchester-united-sacked</link>
      <description><p>Disastrous decisions and confused appointments have been a constant theme at Old Trafford since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013</p><p>For a window into the alarming dysfunction at Manchester United that Michael Carrick failed to manage and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/michael-carrick-sacked-manchester-united-mauricio-pochettino">caused his sacking</a>, consider the case of Eddie Howe, initially a favourite to succeed the 45-year-old before Mauricio Pochettino’s emergence as the chosen one.</p><p>The former Newcastle manager had been Jason Wilcox’s choice to take over from Carrick. Howe was also the favoured candidate of Dan Ashworth, Wilcox’s predecessor as United’s director of football, to follow Erik ten Hag after the Dutchman’s sacking in October 2024. Except Wilcox disagreed and Sir Jim Ratcliffe went with Wilcox’s man, Ruben Amorim, and that December <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/dec/08/dan-ashworth-to-leave-role-as-manchester-united-sporting-director">Ashworth departed</a> only five months after joining.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/michael-carrick-manchester-united-sacked">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/football-club-most-international-captains-same-team-the-knowledge</link>
      <description><p>Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers</p><ul><li><p><a href="mailto:knowledge@theguardian.com"><strong>Mail us</strong></a><strong> with all of your questions and answers</strong></p></li></ul><p><strong>“Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?”</strong> asks MH Zahid. <strong>“Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?”</strong></p><p>A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at <em>that</em> time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/football-club-most-international-captains-same-team-the-knowledge">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/is-no-10-still-the-best-or-no-41-the-myths-and-maths-of-premier-league-shirt-numbers</link>
      <description><p>While No 9s still score the most goals and No 1s try to stop them, trends have changed since the introduction of squad numbers in the early 1990s</p><p>How much is a shirt number worth? It costs £8 if you want two digits added to the back of Arsenal’s 2026-27 home shirt, whereas Manchester City add on £16 for customisation, whether you want a name as well as a number or not.</p><p>That is cheap compared to what baseball players decide among themselves. Juan Soto bought Brett Baty a $92,000 (£69,000) car in exchange for getting his preferred number (22) when he joined the New York Mets last year. But that’s baseball, where they allow players to wear ‘0’. Anything goes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/is-no-10-still-the-best-or-no-41-the-myths-and-maths-of-premier-league-shirt-numbers">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Ultimate 1-50: the male footballers best associated with each squad number</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2026/nov/10/ultimate-1-50-the-male-footballers-best-associated-with-each-squad-number</link>
      <description><p>Who is football’s most legendary No 9? Has there ever been a legendary No 28? And why exactly does Mario Balotelli love wearing No 45 so much? Here’s our list and the stories behind it</p><p>The relationship between players and numbers is a long-established one filled with memories and fascinating as well as fun stories behind them. With that in mind, the Guardian has had a go at deciding which male player is best associated with each squad number, from 1-50. Various factors were taken into consideration, including how long a player wore/has worn that number, what they achieved/have achieved in it, why they decided to wear it in the first place and, in some cases, how distinctly it has become associated with them in death. The below list is highly subjective and ultimately a bit of fun, but don’t let that stop you being shocked and furious in equal measure.</p><p>***</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2026/nov/10/ultimate-1-50-the-male-footballers-best-associated-with-each-squad-number">Continue reading...</a></description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a235f704-df5e-11f1-bb2c-85a37d07b862</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:08:48 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg">AP - Emma Da Silva</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France slams Russian ‘intimidation’ as fresh EU sanctions come into force</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261113-france-slams-russian-intimidation-fedorova-as-fresh-eu-sanctions-come-into-force</link><description>
The European Union will approve more ​sanctions against Russia on Monday, the bulk of which were proposed by France, the country's Minister for European Affairs Benjamin Haddad said on Thursday. He also warned that Paris would not be intimidated by Moscow’s decision to ban two French journalists and two MPs from entering the country.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c0a81bba-5f78-11f1-b8ae-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/photo-2026-06-03-19-52-33.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c0a81bba-5f78-11f1-b8ae-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/photo-2026-06-03-19-52-33.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9187c500-de81-11f1-bc9f-6b48e96878ad</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:44:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c0a81bba-5f78-11f1-b8ae-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/photo-2026-06-03-19-52-33.jpg">© RFI</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France requests arrest warrants for Iranian suspects over supermarket cyberattack</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-france-requests-arrest-warrants-for-iranian-suspects-over-supermarket-cyberattack</link><description>
France has requested international arrest warrants for three Iranian men over October’s cyberattack on supermarket fridges, while Tehran rejects the allegations as “baseless and malicious”. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8a8f8ab4-ddcb-11f1-8b47-cfca036f86fe</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:00:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race vowing to expel unemployed foreigners</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-zemmour-joins-2027-race-vowing-to-expel-jobless-foreigners</link><description>
Far-right politician Eric Zemmour has formally entered next year’s French presidential race. He is promising a sharp cut in immigration, and the expulsion of foreigners who are out of work, even if they live in France legally.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e4ed6918-ddc6-11f1-ab44-f53e2031ebff</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 12:55:43 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg">© SIMON WOHLFAHRT / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Emmanuel and Brigitte Macron file new lawsuit in US against right-wing influencer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-emmanuel-and-brigitte-macron-file-new-lawsuit-in-us-against-right-wing-influencer</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte have filed a new defamation lawsuit in the United States against conservative influencer Candace Owens, who claims the French First Lady is a transgender woman.

French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a sophisticated cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel Arkéa involving fraudulent transfers estimated at around €100 million, as the Brittany-based banking group races to recover the stolen funds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d4c86e50-d8f5-11f1-8292-031c66ea2070</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 12:31:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg">AFP - FRED TANNEAU</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>MPs unanimously reject 2027 French budget as political deadlock continues</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-mps-unanimously-reject-2027-budget-as-political-deadlock-deepens</link><description>
France's National Assembly has overwhelmingly rejected the government's draft budget for 2027 after MPs from across the political spectrum voted against a heavily amended version of the legislation, sending the bill to the Senate in its original form and setting the stage for another round of difficult negotiations.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">94610092-d8ec-11f1-83cc-05d8d1a87801</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:19:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg">© AFP/Dimitar Dilkoff</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mass protests sweep France as workers and students demand higher pay and funding</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-unions-join-forces-for-nationwide-strike-as-protests-intensify</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Thursday as workers, students and pensioners joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations demanding higher wages, action on the cost of living and better public services. Nearly 1.6 million people joined the marches, including 350,000 in Paris, the CGT union said. The Interior Ministry gave a much lower nationwide estimate of around 600,000.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d1ac4db2-d847-11f1-8e8e-b39696b484d3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 07:11:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg">© AP Photo/Thibault Camus</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title>L'actualité économique et politique en Europe - RFI</title><description>Suivez l'actualité en direct dédiée au continent Européen - Les derniers reportages, news et informations en continu en Europe, Emissions, Podcast, dossiers sur RFI.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/</link><lastBuildDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:33:42 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Europe</category><title>Pourparlers de paix sur l'Ukraine: l’Europe en quête d’une voix unie face à Moscou</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261113-pourparlers-paix-ukraine-europe-qu%C3%AAte-voix-unie-face-%C3%A0-moscou</link><description>
La possible participation de l'Europe aux prochaines négociations sur l'Ukraine s'est transformée vendredi en imbroglio, la Russie émettant des conditions et les Européens mettant en garde contre « les pièges » de Moscou. Entre pays de l’Union, l’heure est au flottement et les Européens peinent à parler d’une seule voix sur l’Ukraine, bien que les émissaires américains soutiennent l’idée de leur participation à des négociations.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ed0db276-df68-11f1-8132-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26317407259150-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ed0db276-df68-11f1-8132-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26317407259150-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">55798846-df67-11f1-a28a-fbab2e9b8a52</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 13:58:51 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ed0db276-df68-11f1-8132-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26317407259150-1.jpg">AP Photo/Peter Morrison - Peter Morrison</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Le grand invité international</category><title>Donbass: «Ces gens sont torturés parce qu'ils sont ukrainiens», alerte Igor Minaev, auteur du documentaire «Izolyatsia»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/le-grand-invit%C3%A9-international/20261113-donbass-gens-tortur%C3%A9s-car-ukrainiens-alerte-igor-minaev-documentariste-izolyatsia</link><description>
Malgré une série de discussions cette semaine entre Étatsuniens, Russes et Ukrainiens, aucune avancée majeure n’a été obtenue en faveur de la paix, et la guerre se poursuit entre Moscou et Kiev. Un lieu résume à lui seul la rupture entre les deux peuples et l’histoire récente de l’Ukraine : Izolyatsia, une ancienne usine de matériaux isolants de Donetsk, dans le Donbass, d’où son nom. Fleuron de l’industrie soviétique, elle devient après la chute de l’URSS un centre d’art contemporain ukrainien de réputation internationale, avant de tomber en 2014 sous le contrôle des séparatistes prorusses et d’être transformée en centre de torture. Entretien avec Igor Minaev, réalisateur du documentaire Izolyatsia, qui retrace cette histoire.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5a8a05d8-df33-11f1-916f-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/Igor-Minaev-r%C3%A9alisateur-du-documentaire-Izolyatsia-dans-le-studio-de-RFI-%C3%A0-Paris-le-13-novembre-2026.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5a8a05d8-df33-11f1-916f-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/Igor-Minaev-r%C3%A9alisateur-du-documentaire-Izolyatsia-dans-le-studio-de-RFI-%C3%A0-Paris-le-13-novembre-2026.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">04f15eb6-df31-11f1-b75c-951812f940a5</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:32:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Clotilde Dumay</dc:creator></item><item><category>La fabrique du monde</category><title>Sommet de Dublin: dans le domaine de l'intelligence artificielle, est-ce déjà trop tard pour l’Union européenne ?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/la-fabrique-du-monde/20261113-sommet-dublin-intelligence-artificielle-ia-trop-tard-ue-union-europ%C3%A9enne</link><description>
Trop tard pour l’intelligence artificielle de pointe ? Pour la première fois, les 27 consacrent un sommet entier à l’intelligence artificielle, ce vendredi 13 novembre à Dublin. Distancée par les États-Unis et la Chine, l’Europe doit choisir : tenter de rattraper son retard dans les modèles d’IA générative ou renoncer à l’IA de pointe pour miser sur ses applications.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a221e8c0-df3d-11f1-971b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/Le-pr%C3%A9sident-fran%C3%A7ais-Emmanuel-Macron-s-adresse-aux-journalistes-%C3%A0-son-arriv%C3%A9e-%C3%A0-la-neuvi%C3%A8me-r%C3%A9union-de-la-Communaut%C3%A9-politique-europ%C3%A9enne-CPE-%C3%A0-Dublin-le-12-novembre-2026.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a221e8c0-df3d-11f1-971b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/Le-pr%C3%A9sident-fran%C3%A7ais-Emmanuel-Macron-s-adresse-aux-journalistes-%C3%A0-son-arriv%C3%A9e-%C3%A0-la-neuvi%C3%A8me-r%C3%A9union-de-la-Communaut%C3%A9-politique-europ%C3%A9enne-CPE-%C3%A0-Dublin-le-12-novembre-2026.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bf1fab1a-df3d-11f1-8321-d1f4faa1ac59</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:49:13 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Daniel Vallot</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Législatives en Espagne: Pedro Sanchez espère créer la surprise malgré des sondages défavorables</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261113-l%C3%A9gislatives-en-espagne-pedro-sanchez-esp%C3%A8re-cr%C3%A9er-la-surprise-malgr%C3%A9-des-sondages-d%C3%A9favorables</link><description>
C’est officiellement jeudi soir qu'a commencé la campagne électorale des élections législatives anticipées du 29 novembre. Un scrutin dont les sondages donnent gagnantes les droites, à savoir les conservateurs du Parti populaire et les ultras de Vox. Pourtant, le chef du gouvernement socialiste Pedro Sanchez, au pouvoir depuis 2018, veut croire en ses chances de réélection.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b98a096-df2f-11f1-a74f-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316749503721.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b98a096-df2f-11f1-a74f-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316749503721.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">29a9dec4-df2f-11f1-85b1-adb66615577e</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 07:15:48 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b98a096-df2f-11f1-a74f-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316749503721.jpg">RocÃ­o Ruz/Europa Press via AP - RocÃ­o Ruz</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine: les Européens seront présents aux prochaines négociations entre Kiev et Moscou, assure Zelensky</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261113-guerre-en-ukraine-les-europ%C3%A9ens-seront-pr%C3%A9sents-aux-prochaines-n%C3%A9gociations-kiev-moscou-zelensky</link><description>
Le président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, et l'émissaire américain, Jared Kushner, ont déclaré que l'Europe participerait au prochain cycle de négociations avec la Russie, tandis que Vladimir Poutine a laissé entendre que Moscou ne reviendrait pas sur ses exigences pour mettre fin à près de cinq ans de guerre en Ukraine.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2c77cbc6-df24-11f1-a56b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316808764019.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2c77cbc6-df24-11f1-a56b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316808764019.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d65c29d0-df23-11f1-a5b4-b96b5cda1c6d</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 06:10:15 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2c77cbc6-df24-11f1-a56b-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316808764019.jpg">AP Photo/Peter Morrison - Peter Morrison</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Reportage international</category><title>En Turquie, un cimentier cherche à baisser l'empreinte carbone de sa production</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/reportage-international/20261112-en-turquie-un-cimentier-cherche-%C3%A0-baisser-l-empreinte-carbone-de-sa-production</link><description>
Le ciment, matériau le plus utilisé dans le monde, émet d’énormes quantités de CO₂ lors de sa fabrication. Il génère 7 % des émissions mondiales de CO₂. Si c’était un pays, il serait le quatrième émetteur mondial de gaz à effet de serre (derrière la Chine, les États-Unis et l’Inde). Baisser cette empreinte environnementale devient une priorité en Turquie, pays hôte de la Cop31, poussée par la réglementation européenne et parce que développer une industrie verte est stratégique pour l’économie du pays.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2e228008-decd-11f1-a3d9-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/IMG-2233.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2e228008-decd-11f1-a3d9-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/IMG-2233.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d7d8268a-deb8-11f1-a227-4343df448611</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 23:03:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Jeanne Richard</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Logement en Espagne: le Premier ministre Pedro Sanchez fait valider le décret-loi «Maricarmen»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261112-logement-en-espagne-le-premier-ministre-pedro-sanchez-fait-valider-le-d%C3%A9cret-loi-maricarmen</link><description>
Profitant de cette période préélectorale, le gouvernement de Pedro Sanchez a fait approuver un décret-loi sur le logement qui donne plus de droits aux locataires et interdit les expulsions de personnes vulnérables jusqu’en 2031, entre autres mesures. Une initiative qui provoque le rejet de l’opposition de droite favorite des législatives anticipées du 29 novembre. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f658a80a-dee0-11f1-a121-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T171750Z-1682661212-RC2SHOAOKAJ8-RTRMADP-3-IBEROAMERICAN-SUMMIT-SPAIN.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f658a80a-dee0-11f1-a121-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T171750Z-1682661212-RC2SHOAOKAJ8-RTRMADP-3-IBEROAMERICAN-SUMMIT-SPAIN.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0455b6aa-dee1-11f1-8a1a-e50edfaef2a3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 21:52:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f658a80a-dee0-11f1-a121-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T171750Z-1682661212-RC2SHOAOKAJ8-RTRMADP-3-IBEROAMERICAN-SUMMIT-SPAIN.jpg">© Susana Vera / REUTERS</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine: Vladimir Poutine se montre inflexible lors de sa rencontre avec les envoyés étatsuniens</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261112-guerre-ukraine-mediateurs-etats-unis-moscou-dublin-conseil-politique-ue-zelensky</link><description>
Au lendemain de deux journées de discussions à Abou Dhabi entre représentants de la Russie et de l’Ukraine sous médiation des États-Unis, les émissaires de Donald Trump sont à Moscou jeudi 12 novembre. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4555714c-dead-11f1-a770-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-12T132354Z-567071639-RC2DMOAP8WV6-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-TALKS-MOSCOW.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4555714c-dead-11f1-a770-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-12T132354Z-567071639-RC2DMOAP8WV6-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-TALKS-MOSCOW.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7bd9e6f0-de92-11f1-a626-e7abcde26283</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:27:06 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4555714c-dead-11f1-a770-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-12T132354Z-567071639-RC2DMOAP8WV6-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-TALKS-MOSCOW.jpg">© Sputnik/Vyacheslav Prokofiev/Pool via Reuters</source><dc:creator>Henrique Valadares</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine: la Russie cherche à redessiner l'architecture de paix européenne</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261112-guerre-ukraine-la-russie-cherche-%C3%A0-redessiner-l-architecture-de-paix-europ%C3%A9enne</link><description>

Avant l'invasion à grande échelle de l'Ukraine, la ville d'Izioum, dans la région de Kharkiv, comptait plus de 44 000 habitants. Une ville à portée quotidienne des bombes russes qui la défigurent.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4bf9093a-e2fd-11ef-9806-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25035468482581.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4bf9093a-e2fd-11ef-9806-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25035468482581.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7e04c784-de5f-11f1-9fe1-1395aecf8207</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 06:27:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4bf9093a-e2fd-11ef-9806-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25035468482581.jpg">AP - Ukrainian Emergency Service</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Reportage international</category><title>En République tchèque, des manifestations pour défendre la liberté des médias publics</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/reportage-international/20261111-en-r%C3%A9publique-tch%C3%A8que-des-manifestations-pour-d%C3%A9fendre-la-libert%C3%A9-des-m%C3%A9dias-publics</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ddf200ba-de20-11f1-8ac7-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/5a22ab59-aaf8-4567-afd1-9096e7dd7d60.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ddf200ba-de20-11f1-8ac7-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/5a22ab59-aaf8-4567-afd1-9096e7dd7d60.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7ed020e2-de22-11f1-995c-eb6ad27c4ef5</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 22:51:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ddf200ba-de20-11f1-8ac7-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/5a22ab59-aaf8-4567-afd1-9096e7dd7d60.jpg">© Adrien Sarlat / RFI</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Expulsion de Xenia Fedorova: la Russie interdit d'entrée deux députés et deux journalistes français</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261111-expulsion-de-xenia-fedorova-la-russie-interdit-d-entr%C3%A9e-deux-d%C3%A9put%C3%A9s-et-deux-journalistes-fran%C3%A7ais</link><description>

L’armée ukrainienne a annoncé la capture, dans la région de Zaporijjia, de son premier prisonnier de guerre indonésien. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/82792048-ddd4-11f1-b501-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26258542812632.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/82792048-ddd4-11f1-b501-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26258542812632.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9f4399cc-ddd1-11f1-8e8f-1775ffa0715e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:56:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/82792048-ddd4-11f1-b501-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26258542812632.jpg">Ukrainian 93rd Mechanized brigad - Iryna Rybakova</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>En Suisse, la société Infomaniak mise sur des data centers écologiques pour concurrencer les Gafam</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261111-suisse-soci%C3%A9t%C3%A9-infomaniak-mise-data-centers-%C3%A9cologiques-pour-concurrencer-les-gafam</link><description>
Parmi les raisons du retour en grâce des Démocrates aux États-Unis, il y a leur opposition au développement incontrôlé des data centers, véritables repoussoirs pour tout un pan de la classe moyenne américaine qui redoute leur impact sur les ressources énergétiques et hydriques en période d’inflation. En Suisse, la société Infomaniak pense avoir trouvé le moyen de les rendre socialement acceptables et presque écologiques.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4f051e3c-bc1f-11f1-907c-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/Cette-photo-montre-des-serveurs-a%CC%80-l-inte%CC%81rieur-d-un-centre-de-donne%CC%81es-a%CC%80-Roubaix-dans-le-nord-de-la-France-le-3-avril-2025.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4f051e3c-bc1f-11f1-907c-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/Cette-photo-montre-des-serveurs-a%CC%80-l-inte%CC%81rieur-d-un-centre-de-donne%CC%81es-a%CC%80-Roubaix-dans-le-nord-de-la-France-le-3-avril-2025.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">faeff814-ddaf-11f1-92be-f90795753f83</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:02:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4f051e3c-bc1f-11f1-907c-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/Cette-photo-montre-des-serveurs-a%CC%80-l-inte%CC%81rieur-d-un-centre-de-donne%CC%81es-a%CC%80-Roubaix-dans-le-nord-de-la-France-le-3-avril-2025.jpg">AFP - SAMEER AL-DOUMY</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Ukraine-Russie: fin annoncée des pourparlers sous médiation américaine à Abou Dhabi</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261111-ukraine-russie-fin-annonc%C3%A9e-pourparlers-sous-m%C3%A9diation-am%C3%A9ricaine-%C3%A0-abou-dhabi</link><description>
